objective: Walk through choosing and migrating to a new embedding model: evaluate on your own labelled queries, rebuild the index, retune thresholds, compare hybrid and reranking, and keep a rollback.

transfer.scenario: A legal team's search index was built three years ago with an older embedding model. They ask whether to switch to a legal-domain model. What is your plan?
rubric: label real queries|own test set|labelled queries from the team
retune thresholds|cutoff per model|scores differ by model

narration.text: Our search runs on an embedding model from two years ago, and a newer model ranks higher on a public leaderboard.
A leaderboard is a shortlist, not a decision, so we test on our own queries first.
We label three hundred real queries with the chunks that answer them, including part-number lookups.
For each setup we measure recall at ten: the share of queries with a right chunk in the top ten.
The new model's vectors live in a different space, so we build a second index and embed the whole corpus again.
Here's the decision point. Its scores sit on a different scale, so our old cutoff of 0.75 is retuned on the labelled queries.
On our set, keyword plus vector search with the new model, reranked from the top fifty, beat vector search alone within our latency budget, so that's what we ship.
We switch reads to the new index, keep the old one for two weeks as a rollback, then delete it.
